title: Local roots. A wider perspective.
description: Meet Broadstreet, a Camden, SC digital marketing company helping businesses with websites, SEO, Google Ads, and ongoing support for over 20 years.
text: About Broadstreet Consulting: Camden, SC's Trusted Digital Marketing Partner Broadstreet Consulting is a Camden, South Carolina-based digital marketing and web development agency helping small businesses in Camden, Lancaster, and across the Midlands grow their online presence and increase sales. As a Google Partner certified in Google Ads, our team combines local know-how with proven digital strategy to help businesses attract and engage customers through the web and social media. Broadstreet also specializes in Drupal, the open-source content management system that powers flexible, scalable business websites. A Long History Serving South Carolina Businesses Online The Broadstreet team has been working on the internet since before most local businesses had websites at all. We built our first website in 1994 and have been helping South Carolina businesses do business online since 1998. What started as a small operation in Wagener, SC has grown into a full-service digital marketing agency serving clients throughout Camden, Lancaster, and the surrounding Midlands region. Today, our focus is on building dynamic online communities and digital strategies that help local businesses compete and grow. Why the Name "Broadstreet" by Tom Sliker Growing up on the outskirts of Trenton, New Jersey, in a small town called Yardville, I had the run of a very safe neighborhood � with one rule: never cross Broad Street. It was a busy, dangerous highway that required real experience and judgment to navigate. Some people got hurt crossing it. Some didn't make it across at all. That memory stuck with me. When I thought about the thousands of small businesses eager to tap into the power of the internet but unsure how to get there, Broad Street came to mind again. So many local business owners can see the opportunity the web offers, but the path to get there feels unfamiliar and intimidating. That's exactly why Broadstreet Consulting exists: to help Camden, Lancaster, and Midlands-area business owners navigate the internet with confidence. We're here to offer a hand, share our experience, and help you cross over. Broadstreet Consulting Is a Google Partner Broadstreet Consulting is proud to hold Google Partner status � a distinction Google reserves for agencies it recognizes as trustworthy, high-performing, and current on best practices. As a certified Google Partner serving the Camden, SC area, we're listed on Google's official Partner Search, giving local business owners an easy way to verify our credentials. Partner status also gives our team access to exclusive Google training, product updates, and industry research, keeping us current as search and advertising platforms evolve. To maintain this status, we must continuously meet Google's standards for certified staff, service quality, and account performance � a badge that can be, and is, revoked from agencies that stop meeting the bar. That means when you work with Broadstreet Consulting, you get a double layer of quality assurance: our own standards, and Google's. Our Story: From Wagener, SC to the Camden Midlands February 1992 � Sliker Office Solutions (SOS) is founded to provide bookkeeping and secretarial services to small businesses in Wagener, South Carolina. May 1994 � SOS expands into Microsoft-based software development, building custom Access and Visual Basic applications. October 1994 � Founder Tom Sliker builds his first website. May 1995 � SOS helps launch one of the first hospital intranets for a large regional health care organization. 1996�2001 � Tom rides out the dot-com boom (and bust) of the late '90s, registering the sliker.com domain along the way. September 2006 � SOS refocuses on affordable website and e-commerce solutions built specifically for small businesses. December 2007 � Broadstreet Consulting is formed, assembling an international team of developers and consultants to deliver affordable web solutions, e-commerce, and online community platforms. April 2008 � All client websites are migrated to Drupal. January 2010 � Broadstreet rolls out ongoing support plans and adds email and social media marketing services for clients. Google Partner Since Day One Broadstreet has held Google Partner status for over 10 years. Google recognizes us for excelling with its advertising products, maintaining a healthy business, keeping clients satisfied, and employing certified staff who follow Google's best practices. As a Google Partner, we stay current on both Google Search and YouTube advertising � the two largest search platforms in the world � so Camden and Lancaster area businesses always have access to up-to-date strategy. Learn more about our Google Partner certification. What We Believe We believe in the power of the internet to build and strengthen human relationships. We believe technology should serve people � not the other way around. We believe online communities and social networks enrich the human experience. We believe the future of the web belongs to small, focused communities rather than large, generic ones. We believe the internet has leveled the playing field, giving smart small businesses the tools to compete globally. We believe in the power of the sharing economy, including open-source software. Work With a Local Google Partner Agency Ready to grow your business online? Contact Broadstreet Consulting today or call (803) 575-0564 for a free consultation.

There are a number of mobile design features that are important to consider when designing a website for mobile devices, for example: Load times - Mobile users expect fast-loading pages. If a mobile site takes too long to load, visitors are likely to abandon it and seek alternatives. A slow site frustrates users and negatively impacts their experience. The longer a webpage takes to load, the higher its bounce rate. Bounce rate refers to the percentage of users who leave a site after viewing only one page. High bounce rates signal to search engines that users find the content unhelpful, leading to lower rankings. Search engines prioritize faster-loading sites.Slow mobile sites may be penalized by ranking lower in search results, especially for mobile users. Menus - A typical menu on a mobile device uses what we call a "hamuger menu", which is 3 horizontal lines that pop up when you click on it. On a desktop or laptop computer, however, we typically have a large navigation menu that covers the whole screen. Clicking - There is no double-clicking on a mobile device, and also no mouse-over actions, so for example, to see a drop-down menu on a mobile device, you have to click it, where on a computer you may just be able to hover your mouse over the menu item. title: AI Alone Isn't a Marketing Strategy
description: Artificial intelligence is everywhere right now, and for good reason. It can draft an email in seconds, brainstorm a month of post ideas, and crunch numbers…
text: AI Alone Isn't a Marketing Strategy Artificial intelligence is everywhere right now, and for good reason. It can draft an email in seconds, brainstorm a month of post ideas, and crunch numbers faster than any person could. But somewhere along the way, a myth took hold: that you can hand your marketing to a tool and walk away. At Broadstreet , we use AI every day, and we can tell you plainly that AI alone is not a marketing strategy. It is a powerful assistant. It is not the plan. What AI Actually Does Well Let us give credit where it is due. AI is genuinely useful. It speeds up the busywork, gets a first draft on the page, and helps a team move faster. It can sort through data and surface patterns that would take hours to find by hand. Used well, it frees up people to spend more time on the work that actually moves a business forward. We lean on it for exactly these reasons, and it makes us better at what we do. Where AI Falls Short Here is the part the hype leaves out. AI does not know your business. It does not understand why a customer in Camden chooses you over the shop down the road, or what makes your story different from every competitor typing the same prompts into the same tools. It cannot tell you which idea is actually worth pursuing, and it will hand you something generic with total confidence, mistakes and all. Left on its own, AI produces a lot of content that sounds fine and says nothing. Sameness is not a strategy. Marketing Is Still a Human Story Good marketing was never really about cranking out more content. It is the story you tell to the people you want to serve, told well enough that it resonates and they pass it on. That takes judgment. It takes knowing your audience, your market, and your goals, and shaping a message that fits all three. A tool can help you say it faster, but it cannot decide what is worth saying. That part is human, and it always will be. The Difference Is in the People Behind the Tools This is where the real value lives. It still takes experienced marketers, developers, and designers to turn AI's raw output into something that actually grows a business. The marketer sets the strategy and knows the audience. The developer makes sure the technology works and the website performs. The designer makes it look like you and feel trustworthy. AI can support every one of those roles, but it cannot replace the experience and instinct behind them. How Broadstreet Uses AI the Right Way Our approach is simple: we combine the latest AI tools with real-world expertise. We let AI do what it is good at, the speed and the heavy lifting, and we bring the strategy, the local knowledge, and the human eye that make the work effective. As a Camden, SC digital marketing company and a certified Google Partner, we have spent more than twenty years learning what actually works for local businesses. AI makes us faster. Our people make us good. Explore our digital marketing services to see what that looks like in practice. Smarter Tools, Real Expertise AI is not going anywhere, and honestly, we would not want it to. But a tool is only as good as the team using it. If you want marketing that is built on strategy and sharpened by the latest technology, not just churned out by a machine, that is exactly what we do. title: Why Your Business Isn't Showing Up on Google (and How to Fix It)
description: You know your business is good. Your customers know it too. So why does someone searching for exactly what you offer end up finding three competitors before…
text: Why Your Business Isn't Showing Up on Google (and How to Fix It) You know your business is good. Your customers know it too. So why does someone searching for exactly what you offer end up finding three competitors before they ever see your name? It is one of the most common frustrations we hear at Broadstreet , and the good news is that it is almost always fixable. Here are the usual suspects. Your Google Business Profile Is Incomplete or Unclaimed For local search, your Google Business Profile matters even more than your website. It is the box that shows up on Google Maps with your hours, photos, and reviews. If you have never claimed it, or you claimed it years ago and never touched it again, Google has little reason to show you. A complete, active profile with the right categories, accurate hours, and real photos is the single fastest way to start showing up when neighbors search. You Have Few Reviews, or None at All Reviews are one of the strongest signals Google uses to decide who to show first. A business with steady, recent reviews looks trustworthy to both Google and the customer scrolling past. If your competitors have fifty reviews and you have three, that gap is doing real damage. The fix is not complicated: you need a simple, consistent way to ask happy customers to leave one, which is something Broadstreet helps local businesses set up. Your Website Isn't Built for Local Search A pretty website is not the same as a findable one. If your site never mentions the towns you serve, loads slowly, or is hard to use on a phone, Google struggles to connect you with local searchers. Search engine optimization is what closes that gap, and it is not a one-time task. It is an ongoing process of making your site clearer and more relevant so the right people find you. Our SEO and web development team works on exactly this. Your Information Isn't Consistent Everywhere Google cross-checks your name, address, and phone number across the web. If your address is listed one way on Facebook, another way on an old directory, and a third way on your own site, that inconsistency chips away at your credibility in Google's eyes. Cleaning it up so everything matches is tedious but powerful, and it is one of the first things we tackle for new clients. You Went Quiet Google favors businesses that stay active. If your profile has no recent posts, your website has not changed in two years, and nothing new is happening online, you look dormant. Regular posts, fresh content, and steady updates tell Google you are open and worth showing. Consistency beats intensity every time. The Good News: This Is All Fixable None of these problems require a massive budget or a marketing degree. They just require someone who does this every day. title: What We Love About Small Towns (And Why We Never Left)
description: There's a particular kind of quiet you get in Camden on a Sunday morning. The kind where you can hear the birds arguing over a birdfeeder two yards away,…
text: What We Love About Small Towns (And Why We Never Left) There's a particular kind of quiet you get in Camden on a Sunday morning. The kind where you can hear the birds arguing over a birdfeeder two yards away, where the guy at the hardware store already knows you're there for a specific bolt because he sold you the last one, where somebody's dog has clearly decided the whole street belongs to him and nobody's arguing. We've built our business inside that quiet. Not despite it. Because of it. When Broadstreet started, it wasn't in a glass office park with a skyline view. It started in South Carolina, in towns where you wave at people you don't officially know yet, where the local diner remembers your order, and where a business isn't just a name on a building, it's somebody's kid's college fund, somebody's retirement plan, somebody's whole life poured into a storefront. That matters to us. It's shaped everything about how we work. There's a myth about small towns that they're behind. Slower. Waiting to catch up to the "real world" of big cities and bigger budgets. We've never believed that, and honestly, the longer we do this work, the more convinced we are that it's backwards. Small towns aren't behind. They're just built differently. Relationships carry more weight than transactions. Reputation travels faster than any ad campaign. A handshake still means something. If anything, small towns understood the internet's biggest promise, that you could build real trust with real people, long before it had a name for it. That's the world we grew up doing business in, and it's the lens we bring to every website we build and every campaign we run. When a client walks through our door, they're not a lead number or a quarterly target. They're the owner of the bakery that's been open since before we were, or the contractor whose whole crew is his cousins, or the new shop owner who just took the leap nobody in her family had taken before. We know these people because we are these people. We've sat in the same church pews, cheered at the same Friday night football games, and complained about the same four-way stop that everyone in town has an opinion about. So when we help a small business figure out its place online, it isn't abstract to us. We're not translating some big-city playbook down to a smaller scale. We're doing something closer to matchmaking, helping a real, rooted, local business find the people out there who are already looking for exactly what it offers, whether that's down the street or three counties over. Good marketing was never about shouting the loudest. It's about telling a true story to the people who need to hear it. Small towns taught us that a long time before it became a tagline. There's something else small-town life gives you that's harder to name but easy to feel: patience for the long game. Nobody in Camden expects a business to blow up overnight. Trust here is built the old way, slowly, one good interaction at a time, one referral passed between neighbors, one year folding into the next until suddenly you're the place people have always gone to. We've tried to build Broadstreet the same way. We're not chasing quick wins that look good in a pitch deck and vanish six months later. We're in it for the version of success that still means something a decade from now, the kind that's built brick by brick instead of hyped into existence. We've grown since our early days, added new offices, taken on clients well outside our own zip code, learned new tools and platforms as the web itself changed shape around us. But the instinct underneath all of it hasn't moved an inch. We still believe a business is a living, breathing thing that belongs to real people with real stakes. We still believe the best work happens when you actually care whether the person across the table succeeds, not just whether the invoice clears. And we still believe that small towns, with their long memories and their handshake deals and their genuine investment in each other, have something to teach the rest of the world about how business should feel. So if you're a small business owner reading this, wherever you are, know that the folks helping you online don't have to come from some far-off headquarters, running your account like a number on a spreadsheet. They can come from a town just like yours. They can understand, in their bones, what it means to build something with your own hands and hand it down to the next generation, or to open the doors for the first time and hope like anything that people come in. That's who we are at Broadstreet. Small town people, doing work we believe in, for businesses we genuinely want to see thrive. Some things are worth keeping simple. text: From Storefront to Online Store: A Guide to eCommerce for Camden and Columbia, SC Retailers Running a successful retail business today means meeting customers wherever they want to shop. For many businesses in Camden, Columbia, Lugoff, Elgin, and throughout the Midlands, that means expanding beyond the storefront and creating an online shopping experience. If you've considered selling online but felt overwhelmed by the process, you're not alone. Questions about payment processing, inventory management, shipping, website design, and online marketing can make eCommerce seem complicated. The good news is that with the right strategy and the right platform, launching an online store is more achievable than ever�and the rewards can extend far beyond your local community. Why Every Retail Business Should Consider eCommerce Consumer shopping habits have changed dramatically over the past decade. Today's customers often begin their buying journey online, even if they ultimately make their purchase in person. Before visiting a store, shoppers frequently: Search for products online. Compare prices. Check store hours. Read customer reviews. Browse inventory. Verify availability. Look for special promotions. If your business doesn't provide that information online, there's a good chance they'll find it from one of your competitors instead. An eCommerce website allows your customers to shop whenever it's convenient for them�whether that's during business hours, late at night, or while relaxing at home. Your website becomes a salesperson that's available 24 hours a day, seven days a week. Expand Beyond Your Local Market One of the biggest advantages of eCommerce is that it removes geographic limitations. Instead of relying solely on foot traffic from Camden, Columbia, Lugoff, or Elgin, your products become available to customers throughout South Carolina�and even across the country. For some businesses, online sales become an additional revenue stream. For others, they become the primary source of growth. A great local example is Busbee Truck Parts, one of our long-time clients. What began as a small, two-person body shop grew into an internationally recognized business by embracing eCommerce and making its products available to customers far beyond South Carolina. While every business won't ship products worldwide, every retailer has the opportunity to reach more customers than their storefront alone could ever serve. What Makes a Successful Online Store? A successful eCommerce website is much more than an online catalog. It should make shopping simple, secure, and enjoyable from the moment a customer lands on your website until they complete their purchase. Some of the most important features include: Easy-to-navigate product categories. High-quality product photos. Detailed product descriptions. Simple search functionality. Fast page loading. Mobile-friendly design. Secure checkout. Clear shipping information. Customer account options. Easy contact information. Every step should help customers feel confident about making a purchase. Security Builds Customer Confidence Trust is one of the most important parts of selling online. Customers need to know their personal and payment information is protected. Your online store should include: Secure HTTPS encryption. Trusted payment gateways. PCI-compliant payment processing. Secure customer accounts. Regular software updates. A secure website not only protects your customers�it also protects your business and helps build credibility with search engines. Choose an eCommerce Platform That Can Grow One mistake many businesses make is choosing a platform that only meets today's needs. As your business grows, your website should grow with it. You'll want an eCommerce platform that supports: Hundreds or thousands of products. Product categories and filters. Customer accounts. Promotional pricing. Gift cards. Shipping integrations. Sales reporting. Inventory management. Future expansion. Choosing the right platform from the beginning can save significant time and expense later. Inventory Management Matters One of the biggest concerns retailers have about selling online is keeping inventory accurate. Fortunately, modern eCommerce platforms can often integrate with your existing inventory or accounting systems. Instead of manually updating inventory every day, your website can work alongside your existing business processes, helping reduce errors while saving valuable time. Whether you have dozens of products or thousands, automation helps your online store remain accurate and efficient. Mobile Shopping Is the New Standard More people shop from smartphones than ever before. If your checkout process is difficult on a mobile device, customers are likely to abandon their shopping carts before completing a purchase. A modern eCommerce website should include: Responsive design. Large, easy-to-use buttons. Fast loading pages. Mobile-friendly checkout. Digital wallet compatibility where appropriate. Simple navigation. The easier it is to buy from your website, the more sales you're likely to generate. Your Online Store Needs Customers Launching an online store is only the first step. Platforms like Facebook and Instagram allow retailers to: Showcase new arrivals. Promote seasonal sales. Highlight customer favorites. Build relationships with shoppers. Direct customers straight to product pages. Combined with a strong website, social media becomes a powerful tool for generating both online and in-store sales. text: Google Ads vs. SEO: Which Is Right for Your Sumter or Camden, SC Business? If you're investing in digital marketing for your business, you've probably asked yourself one important question: Should I invest in Google Ads or SEO? It's one of the most common questions we hear from business owners throughout Camden, Sumter, Columbia, Lugoff, and the surrounding Midlands. The truth is, there isn't a one-size-fits-all answer. Both Google Ads and Search Engine Optimization (SEO) can generate new customers, but they work in very different ways. Understanding how each strategy works�and when to use it�can help you make smarter marketing decisions and get the most from your budget. What Is SEO? Search Engine Optimization (SEO) is the process of improving your website so it ranks higher in Google's organic (non-paid) search results. When someone searches for phrases like: HVAC repair Camden, SC CPA near me Roofing contractor Sumter, SC Electrician Columbia, SC Pest control Lugoff Google analyzes hundreds of factors to determine which websites deserve to appear at the top of the results. Good SEO isn't about tricks or shortcuts. It's about building a website that search engines trust and customers find valuable. That includes: Creating helpful, relevant content. Optimizing page titles and meta descriptions. Improving website speed. Making your website mobile-friendly. Building local citations. Optimizing your Google Business Profile. Earning positive customer reviews. Creating location-specific service pages. The goal is simple: earn visibility without paying for every visitor who clicks on your website. The Benefits of SEO SEO is often considered one of the best long-term marketing investments because the results continue to build over time. Benefits include: Consistent organic traffic. Increased credibility with customers. Better visibility in Google Search and Google Maps. Higher-quality website visitors. Lower long-term customer acquisition costs. Continued traffic even when you're not actively paying for ads. The biggest advantage of SEO is that you're building a digital asset. Every optimized page, blog article, customer review, and service page adds value to your website and helps improve your visibility over time. The Challenge with SEO SEO isn't instant. Google doesn't move websites to the top of search results overnight. Depending on your industry and competition, it may take several months before you begin seeing significant improvements in rankings and website traffic. That's because Google rewards websites that consistently demonstrate expertise, authority, and trust over time. For businesses looking for immediate leads, SEO alone may not provide results quickly enough. What Are Google Ads? Google Ads, also known as Search Engine Marketing (SEM), allows your business to appear at the very top of Google's search results almost immediately. Instead of earning your placement organically, you bid on keywords related to your services. When someone searches for those terms, your advertisement may appear above the organic search results. Unlike SEO, Google Ads operates on a pay-per-click (PPC) model. You only pay when someone clicks on your advertisement. This makes Google Ads an excellent option for businesses that need visibility right away. The Benefits of Google Ads One of the biggest advantages of Google Ads is speed. A professionally managed campaign can begin generating website traffic and phone calls almost immediately after launch. Google Ads also offers exceptional targeting. You can choose: The exact cities or counties where your ads appear. The keywords that trigger your advertisements. The days and hours your ads run. The services you want to promote. Your daily advertising budget. For businesses serving Camden, Sumter, Columbia, Lugoff, Elgin, or Kershaw County, this level of targeting ensures your advertising dollars are focused on customers who are actually within your service area. Google Ads Works Especially Well For Google Ads can be particularly effective for: New businesses without established search rankings. Businesses launching a new service. Seasonal promotions. Emergency service providers. Highly competitive industries. Companies entering a new market. Businesses looking to generate leads immediately. If you need your phone ringing this week rather than six months from now, Google Ads often provides the fastest path. The Downsides of Google Ads While Google Ads can produce quick results, they stop producing traffic when you stop paying. Think of it like renting a billboard. As long as you pay for the space, your advertisement remains visible. Once the campaign ends, so does the visibility. That's why relying exclusively on paid advertising can become expensive over the long term. Without a strong website and ongoing SEO efforts, you'll continue paying for every new visitor indefinitely. SEO vs. Google Ads: A Side-by-Side Comparison SEO Google Ads Builds long-term visibility Generates immediate visibility Organic (non-paid) traffic Pay-per-click advertising Takes months to build momentum Can begin generating leads almost immediately Builds authority and trust Excellent for promotions and fast growth Long-term return on investment Highly controllable daily budgets Continues generating traffic over time Traffic stops when campaigns stop Neither strategy is inherently better�they simply solve different business challenges. Why Most Local Businesses Benefit From Both The strongest digital marketing strategies don't force you to choose between SEO and Google Ads. Instead, they use each where it performs best. Think of SEO as building equity in your home. Every optimized webpage, customer review, blog article, and local citation increases the long-term value of your online presence. Google Ads, on the other hand, is like renting a home while you're building your own. It gives you immediate visibility while your long-term investment grows. As your SEO begins producing more organic traffic, many businesses find they can reduce their advertising spend for certain keywords while continuing to generate leads through their organic rankings. Together, SEO and Google Ads create a balanced marketing strategy that delivers immediate results today while building sustainable growth for tomorrow. Which Strategy Is Right for Your Business? The answer depends on several factors, including: Your marketing goals. Your budget. Your competition. Your industry. How quickly you need new leads. Whether your business is established or just getting started. Every business is different, which is why a customized strategy often delivers better results than following a generic marketing formula. text: 3 Great, Simple Ways to Increase Your Online Presence I'm tired of the generic terms I see listed as ways to improve your online presence. "SEO, Social Media, Blogs, Link Sharing," etc. These are all very broad terms that go much, much deeper. To learn how to do it right will take years of research and experience. For those of you who honestly want just a few, simple techniques to improve your online presence, here it is. Clear call to action. Keep your visitors engaged. A call to action (CTA) is a set of words, graphics, or buttons that prompt a user to take immediate action or continue on an intended path toward completing your end goal. Every website should have a clear purpose, some goal they want their users to complete. And it should be obvious to both the business, and the consumer. As an example, last month we did some major revamping of one of our sites. We realized that our call to action could be a litte... louder. This call to action is what the search engine ad links to now when they search for terms related to Isuzu Trucks. It's very clear - if you are shopping for an Isuzu truck, call now, or request a specific part. Now the customer is less likely to waste time searching the site, get distracted and leave, and more likely to call, talk to someone they like, find a product they want, and make a quick purchase. So ask yourself �What do I want a user to do once they�ve reached my site?� Do you want them to fill out a contact form, download more information, or sign up for a monthly newsletter? Start improving the online presence of your business by creating objectives and goals that will keep visitor engaged on your website. Related: 7 Core Components of an Exceptional Email Visual Imagery. It�s all about the images. Visual imagery is the use of vivid and expressive images that fuel emotions and keep visitors engaged. Images are a great way to evoke emotion, and emotion is a great tool to use when trying to convince someone to do something. Think of when you're driving down the interstate, and you see a billboard for a restaurant. Suddenly you realize you're hungry. But then you go a little further and see a billboard with a steak on it, and you realize you are craving a steak. So you stop there, and get a steak. We recently did a site for a local restaurant, and by making the time for our professional photographer to come take pictures of their food, we were able to create a delicious site. But please note , choosing the wrong images can be devasting to your business's appearance and credibility. Don't make the mistake of choosing bad stock images or bland graphics. Good images = enhance credibility, make your site look professional, engage consumers. Bad images = blurry, easy to ignore, don't relate to your content/business, have no real purpose. Keep Your Site Up-to-Date. Keep the content fresh. Update the look and feel. Updating a website can mean totally revamping the look and feel of your website or simply updating or removing existing content that is no longer relevant. An out-of-date site is a quick way to loose your credibility and more importantly, potential visitors. If your current site design is inching towards 2-3 years old, it maybe time for a refresh. For example, we are currently updating our sites to drupal 7 as well as mobile friendly sites. This keeps the site fresh and appealing. If your site looks like it was created in the 90's, it's time to do an update. Many of our site are commerce sites. If we let the site sit with old products and don't continue updating the online inventory, consumers will quit coming back to the site. Our restaurant sites continually need updated menus, specials and wine lists. Related: Building Mobile-Friendly Websites using Drupal Every website should create a great first impression. Spend time researching current trends and revisit the goals of your website, or get in touch with someone who does this kind of thing every day. text: 5 Key Steps To Getting Your Home Business Found Online With over 28 million small businesses in the U.S. - more than 52% of these small businesses are home based, according to the Small Business Administration If you are considering or are in the process of starting a business from home, it�s crucial to get your business found online in order to set yourself up for success. Set Up Social Media Accounts It�s imperative for your business to be on Facebook, Twitter, LinkedIn, Instagram, Youtube & other social media sites. You may not feel like it�s a necessity for your business, but it is. You don�t need to actively update every single one of these many accounts, but you do need to try them all and see what�s best for you, and then focus on growing that account. You may not have a lot of followers or any very good content to share right now, but the sooner you start, the sooner you�ll have a chance of getting there. Social media gives you the opportunity to share links to your website, share news about your business, connect with customer�s, earn new customer for free and advertise for cheap. It�s crucial to being found online that your home business at the very least has a profile with some information about the business, some photos, a link to your website and a phone number. 4. Link-Sharing & External Link-Building Sharing your links on social media and on other websites & forums is important to getting your home business found online because links are a major factor in how Google ranks Web pages. According to Google, "In general, webmasters can improve the rank of their sites by increasing the number of high-quality sites that link to their pages." Getting external pages to link to a page on your website is huge in search engine optimization (SEO). Building links can be difficult and very time-consuming - so it�s important that you do some research into best practices before getting started so that you don�t waste your time. There are several different link building strategies used to get external websites to link to yours: Content Creation & Promotion - Create compelling content that people will want to reference and link to, and tell people about it. Submissions - Submit your news to press releases, submit your site to directories, etc. Reviews & Mentions - Put your product, service, or site in front of influential bloggers. Links from Friends & Partners - Get people you know and people you work with to link to your site The biggest thing to note when putting your time into link building is this: A link from an authoratative website like the New York Times will help your website out far better than a link from a newly built website. That�s not to say those links aren�t important - just know where to focus your time. 5. Intelligent Internal Link Building Building content on your site is one of the best and simplest ways to be sure to be found online. You want to be careful here, though, not to go crazy creating content that no one cares about. Bad content can have a negative effect on your search results. But good content can change everything. When you create a new page, blog post, contact form, product, etc - you need to make sure to build multiple links to it from other pages of your website - not only so your visitors can easily find it, but also for search-engine optimization (SEO). The key to intelligent internal link building is keyword research. You want to link pages using targeted keywords in the anchor text (this is the text that you decide to link to other content) - you do this by linking to content using the keywords that you discovered. It�s crucial that the content is related to that keyword phrase. To help you be sure that you're linking to the right pages with the right anchor text, it helps to earch your site for mentions of similar keyword variations, the pages that pop up may be the best places to add links to your new content. Example : You created a new blog post - How To Increase Sales in 1 Month. Search your site for the term �Increase sales� - say you have 3 other blog posts about increasing sales, these would be great places to add links to your newest blog post. Be sure that the anchor text you to choose to link from includes the words �increase� and �sales�. title: 5 Tips for Succeeding in Google AdWords
description: In my 4 years of working with Google AdWords, I�ve had plenty of time to make mistakes and learn from them - over, and over and over again. Through…
text: 5 Tips for Succeeding in Google AdWords Learn how to set up a new Google AdWords account for success In my 4 years of working with Google AdWords, I�ve had plenty of time to make mistakes and learn from them - over, and over and over again. Through mistakes, thorough research and training, I�ve been able to gain a basic understanding of how to set up a new Google AdWords account for success. 1. Customized Landing Pages Creating custom landing pages can be a lot of work! It�s easy to skip over this step - decide to get back to it later, or settle with what you currently have for a landing page. But that, my friend, is a huge no-no! If you�re going in it at all, go in it to win it. Go big, or go home. Now is not the time to play around with your money. Figure out a good design for your landing pages that will help you get one specific message across with a clear call to action for your visitors. If you pay Google $1.75 for someone to click on an ad, and then they show up to a page that isn�t specific, isn�t clear, and doesn�t tell them what to do next, they have a high probability of leaving immediately. Not only did you waste a click and the cost of that click, you�ve now got other issues to worry about. Google�s going to see that the people clicking on this ad don�t like what they see - so it will cost even more to show up high in the search engine. Your keyword will get a low quality score which will also increase cost. And like a domino effect, it will keep causing trouble for your new AdWords account. Take the time and get your landing page set up right before taking your AdWords campaign live. 2. Small & Specific Adgroups Many clients come to us with an adwords account that they attempted to build themselves and I see immediately why they never got any leads - they have 1 campaign, with 1 adgroup, and 50 keywords that don�t relate at all. When you set your AdWords campaigns up, you want to be as specific as possible for each service you are trying to sell. Each campaign should be it�s own service that you offer, and the adgroups within should be grouped by specific keywords & keyword phrases that people will be searching for. Example: Client is trying to promote products for baseball season. What not to do: Campaign 1, Adgroup 1, Keywords: hats for sale, baseball hats, cleats for sale, baseball gloves, sports shop, aiken sports. What to do: Campaign 1 - Baseball Campaign 3 Adgroups: Baseball Hats: +baseball +hats, +baseball hats for sale, +ball +cap, Baseball Gloves: +baseball +gloves, +softball +gloves, +ball +glove, Baseball Cleats: +baseball +cleats, +cleats for sale, +softball +cleats, +buy +cleats The keywords within each adgroup should all relate to each other. The ad that shows up for each of these searches will then be related, and the custom landing page will also be related. This is how to set up a new Google AdWords account for success - you�ll see lower cost-per-click, higher click-thru and conversion rates, high quality scores & more benefits. 3. Targeted Keywords (Say NO to Broad!) Once you have these well-structured AdWords campaigns set up, it�s time to fill it with keywords. A successful adgroup is going to have 5 - 25 keywords that relate. In order to have a successful AdWords account, it�s so important that you keep your keywords very targeted. There are 4 ways to target your keywords - or 4 �match types� as Google calls them. Broad Match - enter a keyword or phrase and your ad will show up for that term or anything Google thinks is relatable: baseball hats Columbia Broad match modifier - add a plus sign to tell Google which important keywords must be included in the search query: +baseball +hats Columbia Phrase Match - use quotation marks to tell Google that an entire phrase must be included in the search query: �baseball hats Columbia� Exact Match - use brackets to tell Google that the search query must match this keyword or phrase exactly: [baseball hats Columbia] The different match types allow you to target your keyword for a broader or narrower range of actual searches. Broad is the most broad in terms of what searches trigger your ad. For example, if you add "baseball hats Columbia" as a broad match keyword, you are telling AdWords to show your ad for searches containing that term or a similar one. The problem - similar phrases aren�t always that similar. You�re trying to sell baseball hats in Columbia - but writing your keywords this way will have you showing up for search terms like cowboy hats, fedora hats, rain hats, safari hats, etc. You are guaranteed to waste money. Broad Match Modifier is the best choice for starting out. In order to have a broad match modifier keyword, you simply add a plus sign in front of each keyword you want it applied to in the keyword phrase. An example is +baseball +Hats. Or +baseball +hats near me. This plus sign tells Google that you want your ad to appear only if that exact keyword (singular or plural) is in the search query. This gives you more flexibility than phrase and exact match types, but also lets you narrow down your audience much more than broad match. 4. Negative Keywords Negative keywords prevent your ad from being showing when a user searches a certain keyword or phrase. It�s important that you go ahead and add some negative keywords when you start your first campaign so you are immediately headed for success. Example: When you add "free" as a negative keyword to your campaign or ad group, you tell AdWords not to show your ad for any search containing the term "free." On the Display Network, your ad is less likely to appear on a site when your negative keywords match the site's content. If you use broad match or broad match modifier, you should add words you know you don�t want to show up for such as cheap, coupon, free, pornography, and so on. Going off of our previous example with hats, you would want to add cowboy, fedora, rain, safari, etc. You then want to constantly watch and see what people are searching for when they click on your ads, and continue to add negative keywords to ensure you are spending your money on keywords that will lead to sales. 5. Conversion tracking If you don�t set up conversion tracking from the start, you won�t know how many clicks actually became leads. You are then running a campaign focused only on getting clicks. This is going to waste a lot of money. Tracking conversions will help you figure out which keywords, ads and landing pages perform the best. You will see which ones are bringing people in who are actually interested in taking the next step, after clicking on your website. text: Using Google Street View and a 360 Spherical Camera to Showcase your Small Business I recently picked up a Ricoh Theta SC 360 Spherical camera from Amazon for around $200. The camera comes with a great app for my Android phone that let's me setup the camera on a tripod and take the photo remotely via the app. The camera has it's own WIFI hotspot that my phone can connect to in order to remote control the camera and store the output images. The camera takes 360 still images as well as video. This camera and its output are part of Google's VR (Virtual Reality) View strategy. VR view allows you to embed 360 degree VR media into websites on desktop and mobile, and native apps on Android and iOS. This technology is designed to enable developers of traditional apps to enhance the apps with immersive content. I am still looking at the best ways to share and view these images. Google My Business & Google Maps accepts these types of images. You can check out some the inside views of Tyler Brothers Carhartt Store which is located in Wagener, SC. Third Party / Social Sites for Storing and Sharing 360 Spherical Photos Facebook also accepts these images and very recently began allowing you to use these 360 / Panorama photos for your cover photo as well. I tried this and to my surprise found that, at least currently, Facebook would not allow me to set the starting view of the image. Yet when I uploaded the image as a post, I was able to control this. Theta360.com i s a website and app that comes with the Theta camera. Login to Theta360 using the app or on the Web using your Facebook login. I was able to upload from the phone app but never found a way to upload directly from a desktop Web browser. Here are a couple of examples posted on Theta360.com : Broadstreet office with Tom, Jim & Connie Glenn & Kelly & Tom with Harley Here's one of those images embedded on this page: The Broadstreet office. Tom Sliker, Connie Jeffcoat, & Jim Shaw. Wagener, SC. - Spherical Image - RICOH THETA Memento is another website available for sharing these 360 images. I signed up for an account and uploaded a photo. The system seems incomplete at best - not recommending it. https://momento360.com/ There is no actual embed code available, but here is a link to the image: https://momento360.com/e/u/52cb0a0d3a75439fa2c0adea516595c0 Flickr is another option for hosting these images and turned out to be my favorite. Here's a link to my new "360 Images" album on Flickr: https://www.flickr.com/photos/sliker/sets/72157685576174460/with/36453269740/ Here's an example of using embed code from Flickr. When embedding, it only creates a snapshop image, but when you click on the image it takes you to the Flickr page: Embedding a Google 360 Spherical Image in my Drupal Site The coolest thing I've done with the 360 images is learn to embed these images on my Drupal Website. There are several approaches one could take, but here's what we looked at to implement this code on our Drupal site: https://developers.google.com/vr/concepts/vrview https://developers.google.com/vr/concepts/vrview-web Here's the image displayed interactively her on my Drupal site. I am looking forward to using my new 360 camera, and looking for more ways to help our clients improve their online presence with this technology.
